subtype: Approach: trying several hobbies and never settling [Pitfall]
passage: At the community centre notice board, Irfan signed up for football on Mondays, guitar on Wednesdays and coding on Fridays, all in the first week of the month. By week three his calendar was full and his fingertips hurt, his football boots were always in the wrong bag, and the coding puzzle still showed the same error. Coach Harish watched him miss an easy pass. "Your mind is somewhere else, Irfan." "Everywhere else," Irfan muttered. On Friday he stared at the blank screen, felt his shoulders sag and thought maybe he was just no good at anything. He shut the laptop and left before the class ended.

qa.q: Which three activities did Irfan sign up for?
qa.a: Irfan signed up for football, guitar and coding.

qa.q: What did Irfan feel on Friday while staring at the blank screen?
qa.a: Discouraged, since his shoulders sagged and he thought he might be no good at anything.

qa.q: What could Irfan try instead of three activities at once?
qa.a: Pick one activity for a month and return to the others later, because focused time brings visible progress.

qa.q: How might Coach Harish see the missed pass?
qa.a: As a sign that Irfan is stretched too thin, since Harish said Irfan's mind was somewhere else.

grounding: A child begins football, guitar and coding in a single month and, with too little time for each, makes little progress and loses heart.
